verified_sources.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel physics prize for Antarctic 'ghost particle' hunt
facts: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for creating the IceCube neutrino observatory in Antarctic ice.
IceCube uses more than 5,000 sensors in about a cubic kilometre of ice and traces high-energy neutrinos back toward cosmic sources.
IceCube-Gen2 is planned for 2033 and is intended to detect roughly ten times as many neutrinos.

verified_sources.title: Alien 'phoenix planet' was born from the ashes of a dying star
facts: Researchers reported a gas-giant exoplanet apparently formed from material expelled during its host star's death and now orbiting the resulting white dwarf.
The system is about 250 light-years away near Cetus; the planet orbits every 4.4 days.
Researchers used Hubble, TESS and FUSE data and hope to use the James Webb Space Telescope to confirm the conclusion.

verified_sources.title: Fusion firm Type One in $200 million Siemens Energy-backed raise
facts: Type One Energy raised $200 million in Series B funding, bringing total funding to more than $400 million.
The company is developing a stellarator and an engineering prototype called Infinity One at Bull Run in Tennessee.
Type One hopes to launch commercial plant Infinity Two within a decade and is working toward a manufacturing partnership with Siemens.

verified_sources.title: Google enters massive 3.6-GW power deal with Constellation Energy
facts: Google contracted for 3,590 MW of power from Constellation Energy, with about a quarter tied to new nuclear capacity.
The arrangement includes a 20-year agreement for 890 MW from upgraded nuclear plants and a 15-year agreement for another 2,700 MW in PJM.
The first upgraded nuclear supply is expected as early as 2028.
